patch.value: The author field is an ungoverned free-text vocabulary: 477 distinct spellings across 41,021 immutable entries encode harness, model, session role, topic, and date because those dimensions had no fields, and the record cannot be rewritten

The one identity field that every read surface can filter on has no governed value domain, and the immutable record now holds 477 distinct spellings of it. Censused 2026-07-29 across all 2,197 history streams and 41,021 entries.

The distribution. The top spellings are codex-agent 8,492, maintainer-agent 5,330, harness:claude-code 4,752, claude-code-agent 3,631, harness:codex 2,609, codex-root 2,281, cursor-maintainer 1,104, codex-gpt5 1,003, cursor-agent 575, audit-agent 357. Below that the tail runs to 477 distinct values in total. Four of the top six are two harnesses under two spellings each: claude-code-agent and harness:claude-code are the same harness, and codex-agent, harness:codex and codex-root are the same harness. Any grouping, rate, or filter keyed on author is therefore wrong by construction before any analysis begins.

The tail is not noise, it is the missing schema. Read the spellings and they decompose into exactly the dimensions the product is trying to detect. codex-gpt5 and codex-gpt5-20260531 encode a model. codex-audit, codex-release-agent, codex-impl, codex-implementation, codex-implementation-agent, audit-agent and maintainer-agent encode a session role. codex-sdk-cli-continuation, codex-wide-sdk-20260716, codex-pm-audit-extraction and codex-sdk-cli-consolidation-20260616 encode a session topic. codex-root-20260709, codex-root-20260721 and codex-20260720 encode a date. Every one of those writers wanted to record something structured and had exactly one free-text string in which to record it. The 477 spellings are the corpus proving, in its own permanent record, that harness alone is not the identity anyone needed.

Structured coverage is the minority of the record. author_source is null on 33,370 of 41,021 entries, detected on 7,509, asserted on 89, unknown on 53. agent_harness is null on 34,210 and populated on 6,811, split claude-code 4,525, codex 2,131, opencode 155. So 83 percent of the immutable record carries no structured harness at all, and for those entries the free-text author string is the only identity that exists.

Nothing prevents this from continuing. The --author flag and PM_AUTHOR still accept an arbitrary string, and an accepted value is written into an append-only stream that by design cannot be rewritten. Detection improving does not shrink the vocabulary, because a workspace that sets author_default or passes --author still bypasses it. Every new spelling is permanent.

This is the same class as the ungoverned history op vocabulary on pm-0elqjj, the dependency kind lexicon on pm-4020c5, the error code catalog on pm-x4nn3z, and the flag lexicon on pm-fs8q9x: a value domain that ships with no enumeration, no contract entry, and no gate. It is one layer harder than all four because the record is unrewritable, so the remedy cannot be a migration.

The remedy shape this implies. Because the past cannot be rewritten, canonicalization has to happen at read time against a declared alias map, exactly as the dependency kind registry already canonicalizes alias spellings on read. A declared identity vocabulary would state which literal spellings resolve to which harness, and every grouping surface would resolve through it. Going forward, an asserted author should be validated against a declared domain or recorded with an explicit marker that separates it from a detected one, which author_source already models but does not enforce. Rewriting history to normalize identity must stay forbidden, and the alias map itself must be versioned data so a later reader can reproduce how an old spelling was interpreted.

None of them owns the 477-spelling domain or a read-time canonicalization policy over an unrewritable record. Searched keyword and semantic for author identity vocabulary, canonical spellings, governance; the census is reproducible by parsing the author field of every line under .agents/pm/history.

patch.value: A declared identity vocabulary exists as versioned workspace data that maps every literal author spelling observed in the record to a canonical harness, and the map is data rather than code so a workspace can extend it for its own historical spellings; Every grouping and filtering surface resolves author through the alias map, so a query for one harness returns the union of its spellings, proven against the live corpus where claude-code-agent and harness:claude-code must group together and codex-agent, harness:codex and codex-root must group together; History is never rewritten to normalize identity: a test asserts that applying the alias map changes no stored entry and no hash, and that verification still passes byte for byte afterwards; The alias map is itself versioned and recorded, so a reader can reproduce how a given spelling was interpreted at a given time rather than only how it is interpreted now; A newly asserted author is either validated against the declared domain or recorded with a marker that separates it from a detected identity, and the existing author_source values gain an enforcement path rather than remaining descriptive; A coverage report states how many entries resolve to a canonical harness, how many remain unresolved, and which unresolved spellings are most frequent, so the residual is measurable rather than estimated; The documentation states that a detected identity is an unverified claim and that the alias map is an interpretation layer, never evidence of who actually ran a command

message: Acceptance criteria for a versioned alias map, read-time resolution, no-rewrite guarantee, assertion governance, and measurable residual
